name: Rwanda
note: Since the 2024 persons and family law, a death in a healthcare facility is registered there, on the facility doctor's certificate, by a facility officer acting as civil registrar, and recorded immediately in the electronic register. Deaths elsewhere are registered by a parent, spouse or other informed person within 30 days. They need a local-authority certificate and two witnesses, and a burial permit leads to immediate recording. How the record then reaches the national population register and other agencies is not stated in this law.

steps.title: Facility doctor issues the certificate of death
steps.localName: icyemezo cy’uko umuntu yapfuye / certificat de décès
steps.who: A medical professional of the healthcare facility where the death occurred.
steps.trigger: A death in a healthcare facility.
steps.summary: Registration of a facility death is done on presentation of a certificate of death issued by a medical professional of that facility.

steps.title: Healthcare facility records the death immediately
steps.who: An officer of the healthcare facility, who is a civil registrar for this purpose.
steps.summary: Health-facility officers are civil registrars for births and deaths in their facility, and a facility death is recorded immediately in the electronic register of death records.

steps.title: Local authority certifies a death outside a facility
steps.who: The competent authority in the decentralised administrative entities (e.g. cell or sector).
steps.trigger: A death outside a healthcare facility.
steps.summary: For deaths outside a facility, registration rests on a certificate from the competent local authority, plus two adult witnesses.

steps.title: Family registers a death outside a facility within 30 days
steps.who: A parent or spouse of the deceased, or any other person with sufficient information on the deceased's civil status.
steps.trigger: A death outside a healthcare facility.
steps.summary: The declarant registers with the civil registrar within 30 days, with the local authority's certificate and two witnesses aged 18 or over. After 30 days a written explanation is needed. The death record is signed by the declarant, the witnesses and the registrar.

steps.title: Burial permit triggers immediate recording
steps.who: The local authority issuing the burial permit.

deadline.text: immediately on issue of the burial permit

steps.summary: Where the local authority has issued a burial permit, the death is immediately recorded in the register of death records.

steps.title: Unknown person: local authority declares on a police or medical report
steps.who: An authority in the decentralised entities, on the report of a judicial police officer or a medical report.
steps.trigger: Body of an unidentified person found outside a facility.
steps.summary: The local authority declares the probable place, date and hour of death and any identifying details, based on the judicial police officer's or doctor's report.

steps.title: Correctional facility registers a death within 72 hours
steps.who: The director of the correctional facility.
steps.trigger: A death in a correctional facility.
steps.summary: The director registers the death with the civil registrar of the facility's location within 72 hours, on a recognised doctor's death certificate.

steps.title: Copy of the death record for family or interested persons
steps.who: The civil registrar, at the request of the spouse, child, parent or sibling of the deceased, or another interested person.
steps.summary: The death record is the legal proof of death; a copy or extract is issued to close family or another interested person, with appeal to the registrar's supervisor and the court on refusal.

steps.title: Civil registration updates the population register (NIDA)
steps.who: The civil registration system and the National Identification Agency (NIDA).
steps.summary: Law 71/2024 refers population matters to a separate population-registration law; the link from death registration to NIDA's register was not sourced.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: 30 days for deaths outside a healthcare facility; deaths in facilities are recorded immediately by the facility itself.

informantDuty.note: Healthcare facility officers register facility deaths; for other deaths a parent, spouse or other informed person declares, with a local-authority certificate.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Law 71/2024 contains no independent review of death certificates; other medico-legal law not read.

electronicRegistration.note: Civil status registers are kept in electronic form, and health-facility officers register deaths at the point of death.

centralPopulationRegister.name: National population register (NIDA)
centralPopulationRegister.note: A population register under a separate population-registration law (NIDA); its death link is not in Law 71/2024.

governmentPropagation.note: Not established: no onward notification provisions found in Law 71/2024.

certificateAccess.note: Spouse, child, parent, siblings or another interested person.

gaps: Onward notification to NIDA (population register), RSSB (pensions/health insurance), RRA (tax) and the National Electoral Commission: not found in Law 71/2024; the population registration law and NIDA texts were not located on an official host.
Referral of suspicious deaths to RIB / prosecution and medico-legal examination: only art. 96 (unknown persons, judicial police report) found; criminal-procedure provisions not read.
The Official Gazette prints Kinyarwanda, English and French in parallel columns; quotes are from the English column as extracted and are short to avoid column interleaving.
No provision on private-sector verification of deaths found.
